shared_rule: Post-header body failures: when the SDK itself reads and decodes a successful (2xx or 246) response body - JSON, or a binary body the SDK reads for the caller - and that read or decode fails after the response headers arrived, the SDK raises a terminal error that keeps the captured gateway evidence and never replays the request automatically, under any retry policy. Error-status responses (4xx/5xx) keep their status- and header-driven retry rules even when their body cannot be read. Partial streams are never replayed; caller-owned raw readers belong to the caller.
shared_rule_unknown_dispatch: Unknown dispatch: when the SDK cannot prove the request never reached the gateway - a timeout or connection failure after request bytes may have been sent (read/write timeout, connection reset, remote protocol error, abort after send), or a gateway response (one carrying x-agentcc-request-id) without valid x-agentcc-dispatched evidence - the outcome is unknown and the SDK never retries automatically, under any retry policy; the error keeps dispatch=unknown evidence and says to check whether the request was applied before retrying. Failures provably before sending (name resolution, connection refused, connect timeout, pool timeout) and explicit x-agentcc-dispatched: false stay retryable under the retry policy. Explicit gateway contract r4 rows keep precedence; if a row and this rule appear to conflict, follow the row and report the case.
